kind: Stroke-only line drawing (pen-sketch tracing) for the homepage hero opening animation. This file is the drawing the homepage inlines (index.html .hero-draw-lines), byte for byte except width="2200" height="1238" on its root.

source.note: The public 2200 px hero photo already in the repo. No raw or private photo was used.

svg.coordinates: viewBox 0 0 2200 1238 = source photo pixels (no transform); path data rounded to 0.1 px

statement: This is a tracing derived from the public hero photo (hero-fsae-track-2200.webp) of Kefan Wu in the Olin Electric Motorsports FSAE car.
Every stroke was snapped onto a measured edge (or, for thin tubes, the dark centre line) of that photo; nothing was drawn freehand.
It adds no hardware that is not in the photo. Lines stop where an edge disappears into shadow instead of being completed by guesswork; no hatching, no texture.
Wheel rims are fitted ellipses (least squares to the snapped edge points); the rest are smoothing-spline / cubic Bezier fits within about 1 px RMS of the edge points.
Decals (numbers, sponsor text, logos), asphalt and grass texture and the sky were deliberately not traced; the 219 number plate is drawn only as its panel outline.
The live hero still ends on the original photo pixels: the drawing is an overlay for the opening animation and the hero-fsae-track-*.webp files are unchanged.
Two CAD-style wheel-centre marks (the guide group) are construction marks derived from the tracing itself, not edges of the photo; they add no hardware.
method: Edge-preserving smoothing (two bilateral passes), then channels: log luminance (lifts edges inside the black body and tyres), CIE L, a and b (chroma separates the blue stripes, grass and asphalt).
Authoring aid (chains.py): Di Zenzo colour gradient + Canny hysteresis, thinned and linked into labelled edge chains; used only to measure where real edges are.

Curation (author_guides.py): each stroke is a guide built from measured chain runs and luminance probes; strokes are grouped (silhouette, structure, detail, ground) and ordered like a designer sketching.

Snapping (trace_lines.py): intensity profiles along the guide normals; per sample the strongest edge / tube centre is chosen by dynamic programming (edge strength minus a smoothness penalty), optional polarity, sub-pixel peak refinement and median outlier rejection.

Fitting: smoothing cubic spline within a stroke-specific RMS tolerance (0.3-1.5 px), then Schneider cubic Bezier fit (max error 0.5 px) written as relative path data; ellipses for rims and the visible tyre-face arc.

parameters.channel_weights: logY x12, L x1, a x1.4, b x1.4

strokes.derived_from: centre of the traced rim ellipse data-o 0.272 (fw-rim)
centre of the traced rim ellipse data-o 0.344 (rw-rim)

runs.channels: np_cv2 (NumPy/SciPy stand-in for OpenCV's bilateralFilter, cvtColor BGR2LAB and GaussianBlur)

trace.added_2026_10_29: plate-219, fw-far-crown and tsal-lamp: three more real, high-contrast edges read off zoomed crops of the 2200 px photo, snapped with trace_lines.py --only (the other 27 traced strokes keep their 2026-10-27 bytes). Not added: the lower body contour (black on black shadow) and the front wishbones (2-3 px glints), which are not reliably visible.

derivation.generator: tools/hero-drawing/inline_hero_svg.cjs (one run writes index.html's inline drawing, this file and this record)
derivation.why_dropped: The grass/track-edge strokes read as a horizon line over the white page, not as an edge of the car.
derivation.why_guides: Two CAD-style centre marks (36 source px crosses) make the opening read as an engineering drawing. Each sits on the centre of a traced rim ellipse (recomputed from the ellipse's arc data on every --check; tolerance 0.5 source px), drawn in the light guide colour.
derivation.ground_weight: The ground (tyre-contact) strokes are weighted data-w .5 on the homepage (traced at .4).
derivation.min_viewport: The TSAL lamp outline carries data-min-vw="768": it is not drawn on windows narrower than 768 px.
derivation.geometry: data-len = total length (source px, 0.1 px); data-pts = 21 points at 0, 5, ... 100 % of the length (source px, rounded to 1 px); root data-car = tight bounding box x0 y0 x1 y1 of the silhouette and structure strokes (0.1 px). Precomputed so the page never measures SVG geometry; they match Chrome's getTotalLength / getPointAtLength / getBBox (tools/hero-tests).
derivation.changes: group id -> data-group; width/height removed and preserveAspectRatio="none" focusable="false" aria-hidden="true" added on the inline root (the script computes a viewBox reproducing the photo's object-fit: cover at its live object-position). Traced path data unchanged.
